title: The request to the watching tool
description: Asks `mokume watch` itself to do something, as opposed to the other surfaces, which a running sketch answers. This version takes five actions: audition (from now on, a save changes only the preview, and the work's window keeps running the version it has), leave (stop the version under audition, and the preview shows the work's version again), send (the version under audition becomes the work's version, and the version the work's window had stops), rebuild (build and swap in once, as a save does, even when the sources did not change) and restart (start the running version again from the beginning, without building). Placed atomically as ADR-0018 decision 3 requires, and id changes with every request. **A request whose id can be read is always answered**, with the reason when it was declined. The facet exists only while a watching tool runs, and a request left from an earlier run is not carried over.

id.description: This request's identifier. The reply echoes it back. An id already answered is not processed again: the answer left in the reply is the record. Do not reuse an id while the facet remains. **This includes a request that could not be read**: once it is answered, fixing it and placing it again under the same id is not processed — place the fixed request with a new id.

action.description: What to do. **audition** puts the tool into auditioning: nothing that is running is touched, and each save after that starts the new version as the version under audition, which only the preview shows (the version under audition before it is stopped first, so there is never more than one). A save starts a version under audition only when it changes the sources: after a leave, re-entering with the sources still as they were at the leave starts nothing, and saving the same contents again starts nothing either — change the contents and save to audition them again. **leave** stops the version under audition and shows the work's version in the preview again. **send** makes the version under audition the work's version: the work's window switches to it once it has drawn a frame there, which is also when its requested window size and full-screen display take effect, and the version the work's window had then stops. The tool stays auditioning, and the next save starts a new version under audition only after the previous work's version has stopped, so the observation, input and knob facets pass to the sent version first. send is declined with noTarget, and nothing changes, when there is no version under audition to send — no save since entering, the version under audition ended, or a build or restart is under way (the tool does not wait for it) — or while the work's version is still being swapped in; and with notAuditioning when the tool is not auditioning. **Which version a save becomes is decided by the read that picks it up**, when the tool starts that read — not when its build finishes, and for each save on its own (saving earlier contents again is decided anew by the read that picks up that save). A save picked up by a read started while auditioning stays a version under audition: a leave drops it — even while it is still being read or built, and also when it was read while another version was being built — the tool says so in its output and in the preview, and the work's window keeps its version (to show a dropped version there, change the contents and save after the leave: saving the same contents again starts nothing). The exception is a leave that cannot keep the work's version — nothing is running in the work's window, or the preview cannot go back to it: the sources at the leave are started as the work's version, and a version under audition still being read or built becomes that version instead of being dropped (it is built once). A save picked up by a read started before an audition stays the work's version even when the audition is entered while it is being read or built; leaving while that build is still running lets it become the work's version, and the saves read during the audition are decided when it finishes: dropped when the work's version is running, started as the work's version when nothing runs (the build failed or could not start). A save the tool has not started reading when a request arrives is read after it: saved just before a leave, it becomes the work's version; saved just before an audition, a version under audition. A save made while a read is under way can be picked up by that read and takes its role. That window is the watcher's reading interval (one beat of 0.25 seconds plus the time to read the sources). **rebuild** is always taken and acts as a save whose contents did not change: it builds the sources as they are and swaps the new version in once, which is how a change outside what the tool watches (a resource Package.swift declares outside assets/) is picked up without stopping the tool. Which version it becomes follows the same rule as a save, decided when the request is read: asked while auditioning, a version under audition (a leave drops it, as above); asked otherwise, the work's version. Asked while a build runs, it is carried out after that build, in the order the requests were read and the saves were picked up (asking again right away adds nothing, and a save for the same window next to it is built with it once). A save of changed contents picked up for the other window before it starts drops it, which the tool says in its output and in the preview — carrying it out would show those contents in the window it was not saved for. A failed build leaves the running version as it was, as with a save. The build record names it with requested. **restart** starts the running version again from the beginning — its time starts at 0, also under --keep-time — without building: while auditioning, the version under audition; otherwise the version in the work's window. It is declined with noTarget when that version is not running, and with notBuilt when what the last passing build left on disk is not that version, or the tool cannot tell (the last build failed or was stopped, which may still have rewritten the build place) — ask for rebuild instead; nothing changes then. Asked while a build runs, it is decided and carried out after that build, in the order asked; asked while auditioning and the audition ends first, it is dropped, which the tool says in its output and in the preview, as it does when it can no longer be carried out. A restart writes no build record, also when the version it started ends before its first frame (the tool says that the restart failed). A name this version does not take is declined with the reason unknownAction. Further actions are added here by later versions, so a reader does not assume this list is the whole set.
